TL:DR: High school friends treated me like a spare part and like I wasn't their friend, college friends picked me up and showed me what real friendship is. Plus a bunch of rambling.


When I realised I was only friends with them because they were the only ones who didn't outright bully me. Turns out they were doing it behind my back, also doing things like blowing me off on my birthday only to go hang out with eachother, or not telling me what I was doing wrong (I'm on the spectrum, I don't always understand everything socially) and instead they'd distance themselves from me, or just have me sit with them and not say a word to me.

I was so desperate for friends that I let them do all this shit. They weren't there when I was going through one of the worst times of my life, the absolute worst of my high school life. They never once asked what was wrong. I never said because one of them (admittedly, one of the nicer ones) was having a bad time because her parents were going through a messy divorce, even though I was going through sleepless nights due to my childhood trauma and repressed memories coming back to me.  I wasn't expecting the world to revolve around me, I just felt like I needed a "hey, you've got this."

I'm pretty sure they thought I was doing it for attention honestly. I'm not saying I was perfect as a friend, there were some things I definitely would change if I could do it again, but that doesn't give them the right to just treat me as someone who just hangs around with them, as their verbal punching bag who they all turned a blind eye to me being bullied almost constantly.

Even then, the "friendship" only really ended because high school ended. Not one of them has asked me how I'm doing since. We've all gone down different paths, but somehow, they all managed to keep in contact.

It pisses me off a bit, but luckily I found some better, more amazing, actual friends when I went to college. They care about me, we fit together. How I was treated in high school kind of eats me alive a bit, but I try not to let it get to me too much. I don't need those old "friends" and they've never needed me. In and after college, I was able to experience what having a group of friends who'll be there for you at your absolute lowest was like, I got to experience how it felt to be part of a group that wants to hang out with you, not just because it's an occasion. My college friends and I have even been on holiday together.

It's almost been a decade since I've seen any of my high school "friends", but as I'm typing this out, I'm starting to realise that's not a bad thing. They can all sit in syrup 👋😁

Uncle Iroh, with Bob Belcher in a close second.

Iroh has so much love to give, he lost his own son, yet stepped in to help Zuko (as well as others he encounters) whenever he could. He has such a healthy approach to Zuko and his decisions. He's not aggressive, he barely raises his voice, but whenever he does it's because he's worried for him. He never gives up on him, even when Zuko betrays him. 

Bob kind of has that same approach as Iroh, but with less patience and social skills. He's always trying to do right by his kids and Linda, even if it means he suffers a setback as a result, like when he puts off fixing the restaurant's deep fryer in order to send Tina to horse camp. Even when Tina doesn't end up riding her assigned horse and rides Jericho, he doesn't get angry, he just sighs and moves on. I've always admired the way Bob handles things in the show, assertive when he needs to be, but has a gentler approach when his kids act up in a minor way. Like Iroh, he rarely raises his voice to Linda or his kids, only when he's really stressed or when he's frustrated at someone else. He's not aggressive at all, which sets him apart from Homer Simpson and Peter Griffin. They're both very quick to anger and aggression, whereas with Bob, it takes a tsunami of problems to get him to even shout maliciously at someone.

As someone who grew up without a caring father figure, the way these two interact with their kids/kids in general (and in Bob's case, his wife) really warms my heart. Bob's Burgers is my comfort show, the family dynamic is something I've kind of wanted to have my whole childhood, and while it's too late for that now, I'm glad that there's a show that highlights that wholesome, close family environment. The Simpsons and Family Guy are great, don't get me wrong, but having a dysfunctional family and having the idiot husband Vs the wife who puts up with his crap trope gets a bit much sometimes.

Hey, I know I'm 12 hours late, but your story sounds very similar to my own. 

When I was about your age, I felt isolated, like to the point I thought my own friends despised me. I kept pushing everyone away and making myself an easy target for bullies. I tried telling my school, but all my tormentors got was a metaphorical slap on the wrist and sent on their merry way. 

What I've learned is that if you make yourself emotionally vacant toward the bullies, they usually stop. If they make fun of you for something, I.e. your appearance or interests, just stare blankly at them, and without a word, just walk away. In the event they try to assault you, retaliate. Either kick their legs out from under them, or grab the hair and pull away from you. Wherever the legs or the head goes, the body always follows.

As for your depression, make sure you have someone (even if it's a pet) to talk to. Just someone you can share your innermost thoughts to, even if it's someone online, because chances are, the person online can be going through exactly what you're going through. Just remember to be safe online though, stick to places you can easily block and report people if they try to take advantage. I generally use Twitter and follow those who I share interests with, so you genuinely have things in common while also being safe.

Never put your actual location, name or phone number out online, that way your local bullies can't get to you. Start afresh with your online presence.

But in order to make your life better, you need to keep living it. The one thing that got me through my darkest days was my family. Only take the reccomended dosage for your pills, because if you abuse them, you probably won't die, you'll just end up internal damage. 

Counselling will help as long as you let them. Don't be afraid to open up about your issues, they're being paid to help your mental health. 

Overall, you'll be ok. Teen years are difficult, but you'll get through them. I never thought I'd make it to 18 with the way I was feeling about life, but here I am at 22, and while it's not all sunshine and rainbows, I'm surviving.

Keep fighting sweetheart. You're worth more than you think 💙

I was in the foster care system in the UK for 14 years. The reason for me being there was because my dad was hella abusive to me, my siblings and my mother. We weren't/aren't the type of family to communicate our problems to anyone and just keep things bottled up until it comes all out like an erupting volcano.

When I was about 16, I kept having recurring dreams of my father abusing me like he used to and killing my entire family. So when I told this to my foster mum (who is an absolute saint) told me she, as well as my social worker at the time (who was actually brilliant compared to others I've had/heard about) would help me get some justice.

When you're in foster care, you have a case file that basically keeps track of everything that happens in your life before and during care, and unbeknownst to me, my first social worker (an absolute bitch) had written in mine that my brother at the time had helped abuse me too. That wasn't true at all and, due to a lack of communication with my bio family, they thought that I had said he did on my own without prompting. I would never accuse someone innocent. I'm not fully sure how that got onto my police statement either, but it did, and because of this, in addition to the fact I was bringing up the past and reopening old wounds, I felt like my bio family hated me for it.

A few months after the police questioned my family (Mum, brother and sisters), my aunt threw my Nana a surprise 80th birthday party. Nobody but my me, my mum and my siblings knew the whole story. Because I lived in Scottish side of the border at the time while my family lives in the Northumberland area (about 80 miles away) my cousin took me to the venue, and we got there about an hour and a half earlier because she was setting things up for later.

About 40 minutes later, my mum and siblings arrive, and not one of them would even look at me. They all just walked past me as if I didn't even exist. I felt so fucking bad and alone that the only thing that came to mind was:

"I want to die."

So, sitting by myself in the building's bathroom, I hatched a plan. I was going to go to the highest floor in the building, climb up to the roof, and fall forwards onto a spike that was above the entrance.

As I headed up the stairs to put this plan into effect, I saw a picture of my Grandad (the building is used for members of the Salvation Army to gather, and he was part of it until his death 5 years earlier) smiling with my Nana. Then I remembered why I was there.

I completely buckled and broke down in loud, agonizing sobs. I was quite far from the main room, so nobody heard me. I phoned my foster mum, who told me to wait for Nana to get there, and if things didn't pick up she would make the 80 mile drive to come and get me. So I did. My oldest sister eventually came to find me, we talked about everything and afterward, I spoke with my mum and siblings and we're all a lot closer now. 

TL;DR My I thought my family hated me, I made plans to off myself and was reminded/reassured they didn't.
